title: Integrated microbiome, metabolome, and immune cell dynamics in critically ill patients
summary:
This study aims to investigate whether patients who develop ventilator-associated pneumonia show changes in the normally healthy bacterial colonization of the respiratory tract and the gut, in their metabolism, or in their immune system, before the infection occurs. Early abnormalities could indicate risk factors for infection. In addition, the study will observe how these biological characteristics change over time: before the infection starts, during the acute illness, and throughout recovery. 
To this end, we include critically ill, newly mechanically ventilated patients newly admitted to neurological and neurosurgical intensive care units into the study. Samples from the airways, rectal swaps as well as blood samples will be collected over 14 days at  of 5 timepoints. Clinical data will be collected from routine documentation. Study participation will not affect patient management or therapy.
In a second step it will be analysed in which patients pneumonia occurred and in a third step samples will be analyzed using modern methods—including microbiome analyses, metabolic measurements, single-cell gene expression analyses, and measurements of immune signaling molecules. The data from patients with so-called ventilator-associated pneumonia will then be compared to those from individuals without hospital-acquired infections. Using a systems biology approach, the study aims to identify early indications of the factors that increase or decrease the risk of infection in patients receiving intensive care. The overarching goal is to develop strategies for a better prevention and earlier diagnosis of these infections.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Consent given by patient/caregiver (possibility of deferred consent in patients unable to give informed consent at the time of inclusion).
Maximum duration since intubation <14 days
Expected duration of invasive ventilation is to be >4 days.
Duration until potential discharge from intensive care unit/primary extubation and/or start of weaning >48h
Exclusion criteria:
Previous participation in the study.
Ethical inadmissibility of blood sampling.
